title: Center-of-Mass Bounds and Harmonic Extremality
abstract: We study the center-of-mass observable in one-dimensional many-body systems with translation-invariant interactions and extend the harmonic-rigidity mechanism from the one-body setting to an interacting many-body problem. We prove a sharp upper bound on the ground-state center-of-mass fluctuation in terms of the active spectral gap associated with the center-of-mass probe, and show that this bound does not require any positivity assumption on the ground state. In the positivity class, we characterize the equality case completely. Exact saturation occurs if and only if the external one-body traps are harmonic with a common frequency, while the interaction may remain arbitrary within the translation-invariant class. We also identify a natural rigidity defect measuring deviation from the harmonic extremal situation and prove quantitative near-saturation estimates controlling both the variance deficit and the spectral weight outside the first active shell. In this way, the paper establishes harmonic confinement as the unique static extremizer for the rigid interacting center-of-mass mode at fixed active gap.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the center-of-mass dynamics in interacting 1D many-body quantum systems. It derives a sharp upper bound showing that the ground-state fluctuation of the center-of-mass is limited by the system's active spectral gap. Crucially, it proves that this maximum rigidity (saturation) is achieved if and only if the external trapping potentials are harmonic, establishing harmonic confinement as the unique static extremizer.
main_problem: The paper extends the harmonic-rigidity mechanism, traditionally known for one-body systems, to analyze the center-of-mass observable in interacting many-body quantum systems.
main_result: It establishes a sharp upper bound on the ground-state center-of-mass fluctuation ($	ext{Var}_0(X)$) proportional to the active spectral gap ($\Delta X$), showing that equality holds if and only if the external trapping potentials are harmonic with a common frequency (under positivity assumptions).
method: The analysis relies heavily on commutator identities involving the Hamiltonian ($H$) and the center-of-mass operator ($X$), leading to rigorous bounds derived from spectral properties.
model_or_system: The system consists of one-dimensional many-body quantum particles with masses $m_i$ interacting via translation-invariant potentials, subject to external trapping potentials $V_i(x_i)$. The Hamiltonian is explicitly defined in terms of kinetic and potential energy terms.
key_observables: Center-of-mass fluctuation ($	ext{Var}_0(X)$), Active Spectral Gap ($\Delta X$), Structural Defect ($G$), Variance Deficit ($D_X$).
important_parameters: The ratio $\hbar^2/(2M)$ linking the variance bound to the gap, and the common frequency $\Omega$ characterizing harmonic confinement.
main_assumptions: The primary results hold generally without assuming ground state positivity ($\psi_0 > 0$), but the complete characterization of the equality case requires this positivity assumption.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing fundamental commutator identities for $X$ and $H$, deriving a general sharp bound on $	ext{Var}_0(X)$, and then characterizing the necessary and sufficient conditions (especially under positivity) for this bound to be saturated, linking saturation directly to harmonic confinement.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful spectral tools—relating ground-state variances to energy gaps—that are highly relevant in AMO physics for understanding how trapping potentials dictate collective excitations and rigidity in systems like trapped atoms or quantum chains.
